result.question: What troubles the woman, according to her?

readings.answer: That the other woman hid her son after they had eaten hers.
readings.support: So we boiled my son and ate him | she had hidden her son

readings.answer: That another woman told her to give up her son to be eaten, promising they would eat the other woman’s son the next day.
readings.support: Give up your son, that we may eat him, and tomorrow we will eat my son

readings.answer: That her own son was boiled and eaten.
readings.support: So we boiled my son and ate him

assessments.reason: Matches the grievance stated: “But she had hidden her son,” after they had eaten the speaker’s son.
Focuses on the initial proposal (“Give up your son... and tomorrow we will eat my son”) rather than the complaint marked by “But she had hidden her son.”
States a recounted fact (“So we boiled my son and ate him”) rather than the grievance explicitly given: “But she had hidden her son.”

result.reason: The passage marks the woman’s trouble with “But she had hidden her son,” identifying the other woman’s hiding as the grievance.
